newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU takes row with Argentina over textiles to WTO.
newsitem.headline: EU takes row with Argentina over textiles to WTO.

text.p: The European Union has filed a complaint with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) against new duties introduced by Argentina on textile, clothing and footwear imports, trade sources said on Wednesday.
The move, which diplomats said was aimed at stepping up pressure for removal of the duties, follows similar action by the United States last October.
A WTO dispute panel is already looking into the U.S. complaint, in which both the EU and India reserved their third party rights, and should report its findings by the middle of August.
In its formal notification to the WTO on April 21, the EU said it was seeking consultations with Argentina under the trade body's dispute settlement procedure.
The note said the Argentine measures appeared to violate several open trading accords reached during the 1986-93 Uruguay Round of world trade negotiations.

And it said requirements set under the new measures that labels on textiles, clothing and footwear include the name of the importer and the number of the import affidavit submitted to the Argentine authorities were an obstacle to trade.

Under WTO rules, Argentina has until the middle of next week to agree to consultations and a further 10 days to begin them. If an agreement is not found within 60 days, the EU can then ask for a separate panel to be set up.
